newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn weighs sale of Lufthansa in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Bonn weighs sale of Lufthansa in 1996.

text.p: The German government is considering selling its remaining 35.7 percent stake in Lufthansa AG this year to a single investor for resale on the market later, government sources said on Friday.

The Handelsblatt newspaper reported the investor would be the Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau. The manoeuvre would allow the government to book the privatisation revenues in its 1996 budget, the sources said.
"To realise the privatisation revenues in the 1996 budget, place-holder models are being reviewed," one government source said.
The European Commission signalled earlier this week it approved a German proposal for ensuring the sale of the Lufthansa shares would not discriminate against foreign investors.
Air traffic agreements between Germany and many other countries stipulate that Lufthansa remain under the majority control of German shareholders.
